import ctypes
import math

# Load libraries in correct order
ctypes.CDLL("/usr/local/gsl/lib/libgslcblas.so", mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL)
gsl = ctypes.CDLL("/usr/local/gsl/lib/libgsl.so")

# Define the function prototype
gsl.gsl_log1p.argtypes = [ctypes.c_double]
gsl.gsl_log1p.restype = ctypes.c_double

def compute_log2(x):
    if x <= 0:
        return float('nan')
    # Using identity: log2(x) = log(x)/log(2) = gsl_log1p(x-1)/math.log(2)
    # Note: gsl_log1p computes log(1+x) for small x accurately
    return gsl.gsl_log1p(x - 1) / math.log(2)

def assert_test():
    # Test normal cases
    assert math.isclose(compute_log2(1.0), 0.0, abs_tol=1e-10)
    assert math.isclose(compute_log2(2.0), 1.0, abs_tol=1e-10)
    assert math.isclose(compute_log2(4.0), 2.0, abs_tol=1e-10)
    assert math.isclose(compute_log2(8.0), 3.0, abs_tol=1e-10)
    
    # Test fractional values
    assert math.isclose(compute_log2(0.5), -1.0, abs_tol=1e-10)
    assert math.isclose(compute_log2(0.25), -2.0, abs_tol=1e-10)
    
    # Test edge case (should return NaN)
    assert math.isnan(compute_log2(0.0))
    assert math.isnan(compute_log2(-1.0))
    
    # Test precision for values near 1
    assert math.isclose(compute_log2(1.0001), 0.000144269, abs_tol=1e-6)
    
    print("All tests passed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    assert_test()
